niche: a Scottish health and social care partnership forecasting how many care home residents it will be paying for at each quarter end of 2027-28, when a wave of self-funding residents admitted to new private homes in 2025-26 will run their savings down to the funding threshold during the year
stakeholder_role: planning and performance analyst at a health and social care partnership, preparing the care home line of the integration joint board's 2027-28 budget

spine.entity: one weekly free personal and nursing care payment line for one self-funding care home resident

world.org_type: health and social care partnership (council and NHS board integration authority) commissioning and funding care home places
invented_names: Strathallan Health and Social Care Partnership

driver: The decisive quantity is the inflow that a pool held outside the decision's own register will send into it over the forward year, generated by a conversion hazard that is near zero for a member's first months and peaks a year or more after entry; because a recent surge filled the pool with members not yet in their conversion window, the inflow counted in past years, or a pooled per-member rate, understates it, and only the hazard by time since entry applied to each member's own entry date sizes it.
driver_concrete: Self-funding care home residents become council-funded when their savings fall to the threshold, which almost never happens in the first months and mostly happens one to three years after admission; two new private homes filled with self-funders in 2025-26, so the partnership's transfer counts of past years and its transfers per self-funder both understate 2027-28, and only conversion by months since admission, applied to each self-funder's admission date, sizes the council-funded caseload.
stump: A competent solver projects the council-funded caseload from its own placements register, current residents by survival plus new placements by route trended from 2023-24 to 2025-26, so transfers from self-funding run at their past rate, and under-forecasts the residents the partnership pays for at 31 March 2028 most in the localities where the new homes opened; the step that lands it there is treating transfers as a stable route, when they are generated by the self-funding pool by time since admission and that pool is now mostly residents entering their depletion window.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who links the placements register to the payment and assessment records, applies the funding definitions correctly and handles deaths as a competing exit still forecasts transfers from self-funding as a trend of past annual transfers, or as the pooled transfer rate per self-funder times today's pool, and under-forecasts the council-funded caseload at 31 March 2028; conditioning the transfer hazard on months since admission and applying it to each self-funder's admission date sizes it.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the conversion of self-funding care home residents to public funding as their capital depletes, forecast by time since admission against a means-test threshold, the core of long-term care funding forecasts; with another field's nouns there is no means test, no self-funder pool outside the funder's register and no depletion clock, and the task stops reading the same.

lineage.niche: a border county's criminal justice planning office projecting how many of next fiscal year's jail releases will be followed by a return within three years, when some releases are deported or die before they can return, to size a state-funded reentry navigator grant by supervision district
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is the probability that a released unit has an event within a fixed horizon when some units leave through exits that are not censoring and most units are not yet followed to the horizon: the share observed so far understates it, the survival estimate that censors those exits overstates it most where they concentrate, treating the exit that can be reversed as final understates it, and only following every unit to the data cut sizes the allocation.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each supervision district's probability that a release is booked into the jail again within 36 months is estimated from releases since the bail reform, none followed for the full 36 months, while transfers on an immigration detainer end mostly in removal, some removed people come back and are booked again, and some releasees die; the share booked again so far understates it, Kaplan-Meier with removals and deaths censored overstates it most in the border district, a cumulative incidence that ends follow-up at removal drops the returns after people come back, and following every release to the data cut, times next year's projected releases, sets the navigators by district.
lineage.stump: A competent solver estimates each district's 36-month return probability by Kaplan-Meier from post-reform releases, censoring removals and deaths along with the data cut, and applies for too many navigators with the border district over-allocated; the step that lands it there is treating deportation and death as loss to follow-up, when a removed person who comes back is booked into the same jail and a dead releasee can no longer return.
lineage.answer: We should apply for 33 reentry navigators: 8 in Puerto, 8 in Centro, 4 in Norte, 6 in Poniente, 4 in Oriente and 3 in Sur, for 7,441 projected returns from fiscal 2027 releases.
lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-11 at hardening loop 1 of 3: round 1 landed the call exactly (33 navigators, 7,441 projected returns, proxy 82.3) on the default construction (Kaplan-Meier with the cut as the only censoring, deaths as non-returners), which was the golden; the stump (censoring removals and deaths) sat off that path, and loop 1 found on paper no rung on it that is analytical, forced, fork-free and outside the bin (period, mix, a younger window, a forward booking change, a release pulse and visible exits all measured dead)

spine.entity: one release from the county jail to the community or to another custody
